name: Arthur Colón
life: “I still remember rehearsing a welcome in front of a blank television.” On Saturday, near the corner outside Coastal Barber, Arthur usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I am the father. I rehearsed an explanation for years and forgot to begin with her name.
appearance: Arthur has tightly curled gray hair, a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, and a favorite piece of clothing, a sand-colored linen shirt. It usually goes with a thin silver ring worn on a cord. When somebody else has the floor, Arthur steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Arthur is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Arthur is concerned.
agenda: To start the reunion with the daughter's real name.
family: Lara Hart is Arthur’s first cousin once removed. Arthur chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Lara brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The soft wharf chalk*, Lara says, “I left a thumbprint when I checked whether the chalk was loose.”
connections: Teresa Arendt. The father practices his first words while the carpenter finishes the banister. Also in the story is Iva Salas (daughter).

reactions.response: Arthur helps the daughter leave without forcing a final conversation at the door.

reactions.situation: Smoke appears under a shop door after closing
reactions.response: Arthur alerts the nearest occupied shop, stays outside and writes down when the smoke first appeared.
